值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解由靈游坊打造的國產武俠動作大作《影之刃零》如何在全球引發廣泛關注與銷售奇蹟。
  • 剖析海外知名媒體 Eurogamer 給予低分所掀起的評分爭議，以及涉及政治正確（DEI）的輿論風暴。
  • 探討 IGN 中國對西方遊戲界「政治掛帥與流水線工業」的辛辣批判，以及與慘敗巨作《星鳴特攻》（Concord）的強烈對比。

摘要

武俠巨作強勢登場與熱烈迴響

作者指出，繼《黑神話：悟空》在全球引發現象級風潮後，由中國靈游坊（S-Game）開發的動作遊戲《影之刃零》（Phantom Blade Zero）再次引起龐大關注。本作結合了傳統功夫電影的行雲流水與極具視覺衝擊的戰鬥，更力邀動作巨星甄子丹親自參與動作指導與動作捕捉，讓玩家在遊戲中彷彿與宗師過招。遊戲上市前後均獲得極高熱度與優秀成績，許多媒體與實況主亦對其流暢的戰鬥系統與紮實內容讚譽有加。

評分爭議：Eurogamer 的嚴苛評級與雙標質疑

然而在媒體評分方面卻引發了劇烈爭議。多數媒體給予 8 至 10 分的讚賞，甚至 IGN 也打出了 9 分的高分肯定，唯獨知名遊戲媒體 Eurogamer 僅給出三星（相當於 6 分）的評價。該媒體認為其頭目戰節奏受限如同「回合制」，敘事也欠缺整合。此舉引來眾多玩家強烈不滿，玩家翻出 Eurogamer 過去曾對爭議之作《闇龍紀元：紗障守護者》打出滿分，卻對多款優秀大作給予低分的紀錄，質疑該媒體被政治正確（DEI）與意識形態嚴重綁架，評分標準有失公正。

IGN 中國辛辣抨擊西方遊戲生態與輿論激辯

與此同時，IGN 中國在評測中給出滿分，並大膽抨擊西方遊戲界已陷入創作瓶頸，直指西方被政治立場與工業化商業邏輯綁架，頻繁製造「工業廢料」。此番言論在海外 X（推特）等社群掀起驚濤駭浪，引發激烈論戰。許多玩家對 IGN 中國的坦率大表認同，並將《影之刃零》與耗資 5 億美元卻慘澹退場的西方 3A 大作《星鳴特攻》（Concord）相比，諷刺西方部分廠商過度執著於宣傳意識形態，卻忘記了將遊戲「做得好玩」的根本初衷。

================================================

Released two years ago, Black Myth: Wukong sparked a global phenomenon with its stunning visuals, fluid combat system, and unique Chinese mythological theme, leaving many players eager to see what other 3A titles Chinese developers would produce next. Now, another action game from China has garnered massive support from players: Phantom Blade Zero. Wait, what is this? >> Hello everyone, and welcome to Player Confidential. Developed by the Chinese. studio S-Game, Phantom Blade Zero has attracted significant attention since its reveal, thanks to its world rooted in Chinese martial arts, its gorgeous and fluid combat, and boss fights with intense visual impact. Following its official release, the game achieved impressive results, receiving high scores not just from players, but from many gaming media outlets as well. However, one prominent media outlet drew criticism from players abroad for giving it only a six out of ten—though, I guess that’s not exactly a first for them. On the other hand, IGN China stirred up quite a conversation after boldly poking fun at Western games in their review. So. , what exactly happened? Next, Player Confidential will share the events surrounding Phantom Blade Zero with you all. If there’s anything we missed or anything you’d like to add, feel free to leave a comment below. Before we begin the video, remember to like and subscribe to our channel, and don't forget to hit the notification bell so you don't miss our updates. Long before its official release, Phantom Blade Zero had already captured the attention of a vast number of players. Beyond the development team integrating the fast-paced, fluid, and cinematic martial arts scenes from traditional kung fu films into the game—leaving players. excited for the combat—renowned action star Donnie Yen also participated in the game's production, assisting the team in designing the choreography, combat pacing, and martial arts performance. Furthermore, he even participated in the motion capture himself, giving players the chance to go toe-to-toe with Master Ip in the game. But this time, he doesn't need to fight ten people; instead, you just need to defeat him ten times. No. Right, saying ten times is conservative; it should probably be twenty. While the martial arts theme inherently appeals more to the Chinese-speaking world, Phantom Blade Zero has also generated considerable anticipation overseas, with some players.

even comparing it to the controversial Marvel's Wolverine before the game was even released. At the time, famous streamer Asmongold, after watching the gameplay demos for both titles, not only expressed his high hopes for Phantom Blade Zero but also joked that after watching the Marvel's Wolverine demo, he had to quickly go watch Phantom Blade Zero. I think we might have to watch the Phantom Blade Zero preview today to detox ourselves. >> Market research firm Alineia Analytics once estimated that pre-orders for Black Myth: Wukong likely exceeded 1 million units before its official release, with. 62.5%coming from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. The game’s performance after launch was truly remarkable, with peak concurrent players reaching around 720,000 on the first day, later surpassing 800,000. Just 72 hours after release, the developers announced that cumulative sales across all platforms had exceeded 4 million copies, leaving players declaring it was well worth the wait. Prior to this, many gaming media content creators had already received early access to the game to produce their reviews. According to the 45 media. outlets tracked by Metacritic, Black Myth: Wukong achieved an impressive score of 88. Most outlets gave it a high rating between 8 and 10, and even IGN— often criticized by players—awarded it a 9 after 50 hours of play, praising its fluid action, impressive boss battles, and engaging combat system. Seeing this , some players might be curious: which media outlet was the outlier? The one that drew the most criticism from players was the well-known gaming outlet Eurogamer. Of course, they didn't completely dismiss the game's merits; they actually acknowledged its excellent. animation, environment design, and the fluidity of certain combat encounters. However, they felt that once a boss battle begins, the overall action rhythm becomes quite restricted, as players often have to wait for the boss to finish attacking before finding an opening to counter, making the otherwise flashy and fast-paced combat feel like " taking turns," even comparing it at times to fighting a boss with a wooden sword. Is it possible that the Eurogamer reviewer was actually using a wooden sword to fight the boss, and they just didn't know it? >> Can we not do this after hours? >> Furthermore, they felt the game's story was mediocre, with too much background lore and world-building that didn't.

integrate well into the narrative. Combined with other minor issues, they concluded that while Black Myth: Wukong has many strengths, its overall performance didn't quite reach a higher tier. In the end, Eurogamer gave it three out of five stars. This rating disappointed some content creators, who argued that boss battles are inherently meant to be more challenging than standard combat, leading them to mock the Eurogamer reviewer for seemingly disliking the effort required to overcome difficulties in boss fights. But more than the review content, what really upset players was Eurogamer's scoring criteria. Players dug up their past review history and found that. highly acclaimed titles like Black Myth : Wukong, Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, Lies of P, Control, and Resonance only received three stars, making them seem like a complete inverse indicator. As for Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which has been mired in controversy, Eurogamer gave it a perfect score right out of the gate, which is just baffling. >> The result is that BioWare, having received their perfect rating, is now a shell of its former self. >> This led many players to suspect that Eurogamer simply dislikes major titles released in China, with some even sarcastically asking, "Let me guess, does it lack more progressive or LGBT. content?" Eurogamer giving The Veilguard a ten out of ten really says it all. IGN giving Phantom Blade Zero a 10 or even a 9 feels solid, but if a DEI-focused outlet like Eurogamer gives it a 60, I feel like this is going to be a controversy. By the way, the Eurogamer reviewer who originally gave Dragon Age : The Veilguard a perfect score later admitted a year on that they regretted the rating, suggesting that if they re-evaluated it, they might only give it four stars. Wait, that's still higher than other games! On the other hand,. while IGN gave Phantom Blade Zero a nine , IGN China, just like they did with their Black Myth: Wukong review, gave it a perfect 10. However, what truly sparked heated discussion among players was IGN China’s criticism of the Western gaming industry in their review. They argued that Western developers have hit a creative bottleneck, held hostage by political correctness and constrained by highly industrialized business logic, resulting in a constant stream of " industrial waste" conveyor-belt games. They even suggested that Chinese developers should teach them a lesson on what high-quality, content-rich 3A games.

should actually look like. Although many Chinese-speaking players felt this sounded a bit like self-aggrandizement, many still believe that IGN China was surprisingly honest this time. If these remarks were already considered rare for Chinese-speaking players, it goes without saying that the overseas community reacted even more strongly, with the comments quickly spreading on X (Twitter). Some players disagreed with this take, arguing that the West still has many excellent development teams, and you can't generalize the entire industry based on a few poor performances. Some even retorted by criticizing China for constantly pumping out "gacha trash" mobile games, mocking. that all their games look the same. So, which is more appealing: a female character that costs 60 dollars, or a beauty that comes for free? As for me, I’m definitely going for the free beauty . On the other hand, many players strongly agree with IGN China, even calling it "based" while mocking and insulting Western IGN, saying, "We have no connection to Western IGN; IGN China is speaking the truth." Because in the eyes of these players, some Western game developers have indeed become overly influenced by political stances and ideologies; rather than focusing on making fun games, they care more about promoting their own political views through their work. It's so true and. it's what we've been saying for years. Western game creators are politically motivated. They only care about promoting their political opinions, pushing their ideology, and trying to bring people into their cult. They want to assimilate you. They want you to view the world through their lens. And if you are not with them, you are against them . You are their enemy. And everything that is politically correct is what should be normalized in their opinion. One joke, you're done. Some players even compared Phantom Blade Zero to another controversial Western AAA title, Concord, pointing out that despite its $ 500 million development cost, Concord’s peak concurrent player count pales in comparison to Phantom Blade Zero, which cost only $ 55 million . Although they say "you get what you pay for," a $ 500 million development cost is truly unjustifiable. Some players even mocked it, saying, "To be fair, Concord is fully capable of embarrassing itself even without any help from the East." However, some.

overseas players jumped in to defend Concord, claiming that Phantom Blade Zero's high player count is similar to that of Black Myth: Wukong, as it is particularly popular with Asian players . This argument left other players stunned, finding the "Eastern players don't count" rebuttal to be ridiculous. Am I not a person? Am I even a human being? >> After all, players are players, no matter where they come from. Others pointed out that Phantom Blade Zero is a game developed in China, so having many Chinese players is perfectly normal—and it's still better than games that force-feed you content. Even MMO noted that Phantom Blade Zero is a game. primarily targeted at Chinese players, and since China has such a massive population, it’s only natural for many games to have large Chinese player bases . People just be typing. Yeah, bro. Like they're just typing. Like they're not even thinking. They're just typing. With Steam players, 29%are Chinese. Well, there's also the fact that there's a lot of people in China, right? So, it would make sense that, you know, overall a lot of games have large Chinese audiences because there's a lot of Chinese people like... >> Discussions about Phantom Blade Zero are also quite heated. Although many players praise the game's combat system, not everyone is entirely satisfied with it. Besides those pointing out optimization issues and occasional bugs, some players feel the game's narrative delivery is inconsistent. In particular, the frequent shifts between different timelines, flashbacks, and various background exposition make some players feel disconnected from the story. Additionally, some have compared Phantom Blade Zero to action games like Onimusha or Sekiro, arguing that while the game has a rich moveset, the actual impact of. hits and the feel of parrying didn't quite meet their expectations. However, players quickly pointed out that you can actually adjust the pitch and volume of weapon impact sound effects in the game settings, and turning them up completely changes the combat experience. >> Listen to this Ice Blade sound effect. This is the result after the adjustment , take one. Although these issues exist for some players, most feel they don't affect the fun of Black Myth itself; some even joke that while other games start strong and end weak, this game starts slow and goes.

wild. Indeed, many players initially felt the combat feedback was a bit off and found the visuals in the prologue rough. But as they played deeper and unlocked more weapons and skills, they realized almost every weapon has unique basic attack combos and execution animations, combined with cool combat moves and boss fights, making it more satisfying the more they played. Moreover, players have noted that the further they progress, the more they can see the map was carefully designed, with the scale of Chapter 4 specifically surprising many. Thus, the consensus in. the player community regarding Black Myth is simply that it gets more enjoyable the longer you play. Some even joked, "Other developers try to hide their poor work at the end; why did you insist on putting the worst stuff right in the prologue and early game?" Additionally, players find the game design player-friendly—for instance, minor enemies don't respawn, and resources invested in gear can be refunded before it reaches level ten, allowing players to experiment with different equipment and combat styles. Boss fights also have checkpoints between phases, so players who fail at the second phase don't have to start. over. Thankfully this mechanism exists, or I’d probably still be stuck in Chapter 1. Today, Black Myth's Simplified Chinese and English reviews on Steam maintain a 90%positive rate. While the Traditional Chinese reviews started at a 67%positive rate and sparked debate due to mixed opinions, as time passed, the rating climbed from " Mostly Positive" to "Very Positive" at 83%. It’s worth mentioning that when the game first launched, some players claimed it was easy, only to be quickly called out by others who labeled them liars, arguing that anyone who finds the game easy either hasn't reached the. later stages or hasn't sought out the optional bosses. Many have started sharing bosses that took them a long time to beat; for example, many players noted that while they found the boss played by "Sadako" very cool, they also got wrecked, forcing them to helplessly joke that their new controller was just slippery. Some content creators even used cheats to clear the game, leading other players to make memes mocking them : "Classic move—can't beat it, so cheat . What do you mean I'm hacking?""It’s clearly my natural talent and the legacy I inherited." But for a clumsy player like me, it’s a different story; I got frustrated after a few encounters and decided to skip ahead to the main quest , only to realize I couldn't beat that.

either. In fact, Phantom Blade Zero’s producer, Liang Qiwei, mentioned in earlier interviews that although the game draws heavily from Soulslike titles , he wouldn't classify it as a Soulslike himself. Because in the very beginning everyone thought our game is a soulslike . So that's why we're showcasing our fast pace and high speed kung fu action, uh, last year in the global demo tour. But it's not a soulslike game, but it's not a hack and slash either. >> It's something we just combined. different stuff to make a playable kung fu movie I would say. >> Uh, we just take the elements from different genres. Furthermore, when Qiwei was asked how he views the many Soulslike games on the market that use " suffering" as a selling point, he argued that the most important thing is for players to enjoy themselves, rather than deliberately making them suffer. He also pointed out that the reason works from FromSoftware and Hidetaka Miyazaki are accepted by players despite their high difficulty is due to the development team's brand image and the complete experience and expectations built up. among fans over the years; players know what kind of challenges they are in for before they even start. But if other developers haven't built that same brand image or set of expectations, yet deliberately spike the difficulty and lower the margin for error, it can feel like they’re just being obnoxious to the player. Therefore, Liang Qiwei believes that Phantom Blade Zero should focus on using its own game design to provide players with a sense of satisfaction and positive feedback in combat—but wait, the tutorial is making me suffer, right ? I spent three hours on the tutorial, and although Phantom Blade Zero isn't a perfect game, it has still earned recognition from many players upon. release thanks to its fluid, stylish martial arts combat, challenging boss fights, and rich weapon and skill design . So, when IGN only gave it a three-star review, it naturally sparked dissatisfaction, with people digging up their past reviews where they gave low scores to beloved titles, while Dragon Age: The Veilguard received a perfect score. On the other hand, Liang’s critique of the Western gaming industry being shackled by political correctness and highly industrialized business logic , leading to a lack of creativity, has also sparked heated discussions in overseas gaming communities. I wonder what kind of opinions you players have.

regarding the Phantom Blade Zero incident? Feel free to leave a comment below to share your thoughts, and join our Patreon for some amazing " gentlemanly" games!

  • 看見畫面升級、效能退步、翻譯品質與疑似粗糙圖像處理等問題，如何讓重製版失去玩家信任。

摘要

經典重推，卻引發反彈

作者指出，遊戲重製只要改善畫面與品質、保留原作魅力，玩家通常願意買單。然而，SEGA 與 Creative Assembly 推出的《幕府將軍 2：完全版》，上市後卻很快被大量負評淹沒，甚至在不到三天內宣布下架。作者因此追問，這款號稱備受好評的經典新版本，究竟出了什麼問題。

《幕府將軍 2》的經典魅力

2011 年推出的《幕府將軍 2》以日本戰國時代為背景，延續《全軍破敵》系列玩法，結合回合制的宏觀經營與即時戰鬥。玩家扮演戰國大名，透過外交、間諜、貿易、建設與戰爭擴張勢力，爭取統一日本、成為征夷大將軍。作品以浮世繪與傳統日本美學打造鮮明視覺風格，戰役節奏、兵種平衡、攻城與海戰等設計也受到老玩家肯定。

完全版的承諾與期待

作者認為，遊戲能在多年後仍有玩家支持，模組社群功不可沒。Steam 工作坊中有歷史改造、新兵種、平衡調整、畫面改善與新增可玩勢力等作品，為遊戲延續了生命力。SEGA 與 CA 宣布推出完全版，承諾改善光照、材質與環境效果，支援 1440p、4K 介面縮放並更新操作方式，也加入完整中文與日文資源。原版玩家可免費取得尚未購買的 DLC，並以限時七五折優惠升級；未持有原版的玩家則需支付 40 美元。

畫面變清晰，遊戲卻更不穩定

完全版上市後，玩家發現它雖然提升了部分畫面清晰度，整體表現卻遠低於期待。作者提到，簡體中文版 Steam 好評率只有約 10%，英文版也僅約 17%。玩家在世界地圖與戰鬥中遭遇掉幀、卡頓和閃退，舊有問題沒有修好，還出現新錯誤。原本期待新版本能在現代電腦上運作得更順暢，結果反而得在 4K 畫面下忍受低 FPS。

翻譯與圖像處理遭批評

官方中文支援也沒有獲得玩家認可：不少中文玩家認為譯文生硬、疑似機器翻譯，還有大量錯字。原作中的兵種卡、人物肖像與事件插圖雖然解析度不高，仍保有不少細節；完全版放大舊圖後，卻被批評有些細節消失、人物看起來像蠟像，甚至讓原本清楚的角色特徵變得難以辨認。部分玩家懷疑開發團隊使用 AI 處理圖片，但作者指出，Steam 頁面並未說明使用 AI，因此目前只能提出質疑。無論採用何種工具，這些成品都讓玩家對開發與品管流程感到失望。

模組生態遭到切斷

更令資深玩家不滿的是，完全版放棄 Steam 工作坊，改用內建模組平台。由於新版本採用不同技術架構，原有模組無法相容，等於讓累積多年的社群創作難以延續。作者認為，模組正是《幕府將軍 2》長壽的重要原因，這項改動對玩家社群造成直接打擊。至於新版本新增的內容，玩家也指出，部分功能早已能透過模組取得，甚至有粉絲認為模組作者做得比官方更好。

負評風波與官方回應

上市後的正面評論中，有玩家注意到一個帳號在短短幾天內累積超過 100 小時遊玩紀錄，查證後發現該帳號屬於 CA 高階主管，引發玩家不滿。Steam 規定開發者不得為自家遊戲留下好評以影響評價，儘管這則評論並未扭轉整體評分，仍加深了爭議。面對玩家負評，SEGA 與 CA 商議約兩天後發布聲明，承認《完全版》沒有達到玩家與開發團隊自身的期待；影片提供的內容到此為止，未進一步交代後續處置。

================================================

Game remakes use modern technology to recreate classic titles; as long as the visuals and quality are improved while retaining the core charm of the original , players are generally willing to pay for them. Yes, while Capcom and Square Enix are often teased for constantly re-releasing old games, many of their remakes still make me, as a player, say : >> Oh my, that's good. >> Even Ubisoft, which is frequently criticized, released a synchronized version of Assassin's Creed: Black Flag . Although it faced criticism initially due to various bugs, the Steam rating gradually gained praise from many players as official patches were released. However, a recent remake. launched and saw its positive rating drop so low in just one day that Three Kingdoms: Total War might think it finally met its match. That game is Total War: Shogun 2 Complete Edition. Hello everyone, welcome to Total War: Shogun 2, developed by Creative Assembly , a subsidiary of SEGA. Since its release, it has been deeply loved by many strategy game fans. Now, SEGA has decided to relaunch this classic as a " Complete Edition," confidently claiming it was "highly acclaimed at launch." I'm genuinely asking, where is the acclaim? Wait, hold on, where did the game go? >> As it turns out, the game was flooded with negative reviews right after release, and the official team even announced its removal within less than three days. What exactly happened? Next , I will share the controversial story of Total War: Shogun 2 Complete Edition with you all. If you have any questions or want to provide additional information, feel free to leave a comment below. Before we begin the video , remember to like and subscribe to our channel, and don't forget to ring the bell so you don't miss our updates. Back in 2011, Total War: Shogun 2, developed by CA, was a strategy game set in.

Japan's Sengoku period. The game continued the core gameplay of the Total War series, combining turn-based grand strategy management with real-time tactical battles. Although real men might play Sengoku Rance, Shogun 2 is indeed considered a classic by many long-time fans of the series. Players take on the role of a Sengoku Daimyo, expanding their influence step-by-step through diplomacy, espionage, trade, construction, and war, ultimately vying for rule over Japan to become the Shogun . Many players still love this game today partly due to its highly recognizable art style; everything from the posters and UI to the cutscenes. incorporates Ukiyo-e and traditional Japanese aesthetics. Compared to CA's later releases, the campaign pacing, unit balance, siege mechanics, and naval battles in Shogun 2 are much cleaner. Plus, it runs smoothly even during massive engagements. But if you want to know why people are still playing it 15 years later, you can't ignore the contributions of the modding community. Through the Steam Workshop, players have created a ton of high-quality mods— ranging from historical overhauls, new units, and balance tweaks, to graphical enhancements and unlocking more playable factions. These mods have become a vital. source of the game's longevity. Then, in September 2026, Sega and CA finally seemed to notice that players still loved this 15-year-old game, so they suddenly announced the upcoming release of Total War: Shogun 2 Complete Edition . This so-called "Complete Edition" doesn't just bundle the base game and its DLCs; it also upgrades the visuals, improves lighting and textures, supports 1440p and 4K UI scaling, and modernizes the control scheme. It’s worth mentioning that the original Shogun 2, despite being set in Japan's Sengoku period, lacked official Chinese support —it didn't even have full Japanese voice.

acting or text localization. That’s why Sega specifically highlighted that the Complete Edition finally includes full assets for both languages. Do you think they did this because they finally listened to years of player requests? Actually, they just realized the incredible purchasing power of this community. >> Making money, after all, isn't something to be ashamed of. On top of that, before the release, the devs announced that the original Shogun 2 would be removed from the Steam store. As for players who already owned the original, not only would they get the DLC they hadn't bought for free, but they could also get a limited-time 75% "loyalty discount" to. upgrade. But for a player like me who isn't "loyal" enough, I'd have to pay the full 40-dollar price tag to play it . Even though they called it a " Complete Edition," many players saw it as a remaster and were initially hopeful . After all, if you're going to charge players, they naturally expect visual upgrades, modern rendering techniques, and for those long-standing bugs to be finally fixed—maybe even integrating popular mods, like The Witcher 3 did. But these requests apparently proved too difficult for CA. Once the game officially launched, the eager players who opened it were first surprised, then. disappointed, and then...well, let's just say my fists started clenching. The positive review rate for the Simplified Chinese version on Steam is only 10%. Players might think the Simplified Chinese community just prefers leaving negative reviews, but this is a global trend; even Western players are disappointed, with the English-language positive review rate sitting at a mere 17%. The reason the "Complete Edition" flopped is that many players feel it is far from complete. Although the developers hyped it up before release, emphasizing improvements to lighting, textures, and environmental effects—and the visual quality is indeed sharper—.

the problem is that while the graphics were upgraded, the optimization regressed. For a strategy game released in 2011, after receiving a modern update in 2024, players expected it to run more smoothly on new computers, but it actually plays worse. Whether on the world map or in battle, players are encountering frame rate drops, stuttering, and crashes; not only were the old bugs left unfixed, but new ones keep appearing. Players can't help but mock it, saying, "What a wonderful time to be alive, playing with old bugs in 4K resolution and low FPS!" Furthermore, while it claims to feature official Chinese support, many Chinese-speaking players have complained that the. translation feels strange, as if it were machine-generated. It’s poorly done, and you can even find plenty of typos. Additionally, the original game’s distinct 2D art—such as unit cards, character portraits, and event illustrations—while low-resolution, still allowed you to see facial features , armor textures, and even the family crests of various factions. To make these assets suitable for high-definition screens, the "Complete Edition" upscaled some of the old images . When players zoomed in to admire them , while the images were no longer blurry and the colors were clearer, they were left wondering: "What on earth is this? " After comparing the new images with. the originals, many players found that original details had vanished—for example, bows are missing their strings , and people look like wax figures; the same applies to illustrations circulating online. The original version , while a bit blurry, at least clearly showed a bearded man, but the "Complete Edition" insists, "Hey, that’s actually a mask." The strange details and art style have led many players to believe the developers just fed the images through an AI and used the low-quality results, leading them to mock, "Why did you forget to crop out the AI-generated watermark?" Ironically, some players.

took the same images and asked an AI to upscale them with a single prompt, and the results turned out better than what the developers produced. Well, the Complete Edition doesn't mention the use of AI on its Steam page, so for now, we can only question whether the developers used it. Regardless of the tools used to process these images, players feel that allowing such poor-quality work to pass inspection and launch officially reflects just how sloppy the entire development process was. Another issue that hit veteran players particularly hard is that the developers completely gutted the game's modding ecosystem. I mentioned earlier that mods are a major. reason why Shogun 2 has lasted so many years. Yet, the Complete Edition ditched Steam Workshop in favor of an internal mod platform. Because the new version uses a different technical architecture , original mods are incompatible, effectively throwing away 15 years of community efforts—it's honestly baffling . Games like No Man's Sky spent 10 years building a community, but the Shogun 2 Complete Edition chose to drive its 10- year-old community away. For many veteran players, this isn't just a technical choice; it's a direct blow to the community's ecosystem. Honestly, you only needed to do two things: fix the. bugs and provide better modding resources, yet you failed at both. Setting that issue aside, does the Complete Edition actually add any new content? Many players have pointed out that, aside from different cutscenes, things like new playable factions, disabling Realm Divide, or the Chinese translation I mentioned earlier were already available via mods—and fans argue that those passion-driven mod creators did a better job than CA. Interestingly, among the roughly 10%of positive reviews, sharp-eyed players noticed that just a few days after launch, one person had already played for over 100 hours. A quick investigation of that account revealed.

it belonged to a high-level executive at CA. This sparked outrage, as Steam strictly forbids developers from leaving positive reviews for their own games to artificially inflate ratings, even if this single review didn't really change the game's standing. Facing the review bombing, SE and CA deliberated for about two days and made an unexpected decision . They released a statement acknowledging that the Complete Edition failed to meet player expectations and their own standards, so they temporarily removed the Complete Edition and put the original version back up, though this was met with plenty of......mockery and. snark, with players joking, "I managed to buy a discontinued game." Even after they brought the original back, it still didn't immediately quell the players ' anger. From the day the Complete Edition launched, the original version started getting review-bombed as well. Following that, the Vice President of the Total War series issued a statement admitting that Total War: Shogun 2 Collection was not developed in-house by CA, and therefore did not undergo the studio's usual internal review and quality assurance processes. He also admitted that the team was focused on other major projects at the time and failed to adequately oversee the external development work. Although no name was. mentioned directly, players widely believe that a Polish studio called Mardum was responsible for its development and that the project was categorized as a full-cycle remaster. At this point, some players might feel like they've heard this story before, as something similar happened with the GTA Trilogy: Definitive Edition released by Rockstar. This remaster was also outsourced to another company, and it crashed upon launch, with players criticizing it for numerous bugs, unstable performance, and the alteration or removal of much classic content. What angered players even more was that before the Definitive Edition was released, the original trilogy was pulled from multiple platforms, forcing.

users to choose the Definitive Edition for a period of time. As for why they didn't just port it directly instead of using a remaster? How else would they squeeze a bit more money out of the players? Of course, before Shogun 2 Collection, Sega actually released another title that sparked similar controversy: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine-Mastercrafted Edition, developed with Relic Entertainment and published by Sega. It also cost $ 40 and aimed to bring improvements to graphics, controls , and the interface of the 2011 original . However, after its release, players felt it didn't meet the standards of a true remaster, leading to criticism upon. launch. Its Steam rating once dropped to about 30%positive, and its peak concurrent player count was even lower than Shogun 2 Collection, at just 128 people. The only difference is that Sega did not delist the original version at the time, so players didn't have to spend extra money to buy the new version . This situation has led some content creators to question whether Sega has adopted a more cautious strategy toward its Western gaming business in recent years. After all, they have indeed sold off or divested some related assets in the past, so they speculate that Sega may be looking to improve the financial performance of its Western operations. while lowering development costs and upfront risks. In contrast, the remasters or re-releases of Sega's Persona series in recent years have maintained higher production standards, and the titles in the Like a Dragon series are still led by their original development teams. Overall, the reason the Shogun 2 Complete Edition sparked such widespread player dissatisfaction is not only due to the game being riddled with bugs and poor performance, but also the discovery that it used low-quality AI-generated assets. Added to this is the severing of the modding community that the original game had built up over many years, which led players to feel that the Complete Edition was inferior to the original. Now, due to overwhelming negative.

reviews, the Complete Edition has been temporarily pulled by the publisher, and the original version has returned. One can only hope that when game companies decide to remaster beloved classic titles, they will genuinely focus on improving game quality, rather than just releasing a new version that exploits player nostalgia, turning a classic that should be cherished into a commercial tool that erodes trust. 摘要

萬聖節驚喜聯動與病嬌女友熱潮

每年萬聖節，《Fortnite 要塞英雄》都會推出豐富的節慶活動。在 2026 年的活動中，官方除了帶來經典恐怖 IP 與人氣作品外，最引人注目的莫過於聯動了以超低成本締造數億美元票房奇蹟的恐怖電影《愛你，至死不渝》。劇中由演員 Indey Salvestrini 飾演的病嬌女主角 Nikki，憑藉令人背脊發涼的神情反差風靡全球，其標誌性的服裝與經典台詞動作也在遊戲中高度還原，引起極大話題。

推特玩家抗議：消費受害者與道德爭議

然而造型公開後，卻在社群平台 Twitter（X） 上引發部分網友強烈不滿。抗議者指出，Nikki 在電影中是被超自然惡意實體奪走意識並遭受身體控制，本質上是一名遭受心靈虐待與侵犯的「受害者」。反對者認為 Epic Games 將這樣的悲劇角色做成可操控、奔跑跳舞的造型，是在將嚴肅的創傷議題娛樂化，甚至有人憤而呼籲全面抵制遊戲。

荒謬的雙標質疑與虛實難分的論戰

面對抵制聲浪，廣大玩家社群紛紛出面反擊，認為這場爭議荒謬至極。作者與許多玩家指出，遊戲過去早已聯動過無數在原作中身為受害者或極端加害者的角色，卻從未遭遇如此嚴厲的道德審判。眾多玩家嘲諷反對者分不清「虛構與現實」，對虛擬角色的過度同情甚至超過了現實中的苦難，使得這場爭論逐漸演變成網路群體間的文化筆戰。

演員親自破除爭議，以熱愛回擊質疑

儘管網路吵得沸沸揚揚，Nikki 的飾演者 Indey 本人本身就是重度遊戲玩家與實況主。她不僅欣然授權形象，更在社群媒體上熱情分享自己使用 Nikki 造型遊玩《Fortnite》的畫面，對這次聯動展現出由衷的喜愛與支持。演員本人的大方力挺，直接讓抗議者的「代為抱不平」顯得格外諷刺，也讓這場抵制風波在玩家的嘲諷與笑聲中逐漸平息。

item.itunes:author: GamerSecret 玩家機密
item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ohq5FoX32Y0

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解傳奇 RPG 開發商 BioWare 如何從醫療背景跨界開創《柏德之門》，並打造出諸多神作的輝煌歷史。
  • 剖析 BioWare 昔日讓無數玩家沉浸其中的核心魅力——深刻的角色塑造與沉重的選擇與後果機制。
  • 探討 BioWare 近年因引擎轉換、營運方向反覆、技術災難及價值觀說教爭議，導致口碑與商業雙雙受挫的深層原因。

摘要

傳奇工作室的誕生與黃金歲月

作者指出，BioWare 於 1995 年由三位擁有醫學背景的創辦人成立，他們憑藉對電腦遊戲的熱愛，以自研的「無限引擎」打造出《柏德之門》，成功挽救並確立了電腦角色扮演遊戲（CRPG）的地位。2007 年，藝電（EA）以約 8.6 億美元收購 BioWare 母公司。收購初期，BioWare 依舊展現出卓越的敘事功力，先後推出了宏大科幻的《質量效應》三部曲，以及贏得年度最佳遊戲、累積銷量突破 1200 萬套的《闇龍紀元：異端審判》。作者強調，BioWare 過去之所以深受愛戴，是因為其遊戲角色充滿血肉，且玩家的抉擇往往沒有標準答案，伴隨著不可逆的沉重代價與情感共鳴，甚至曾被專業心理治療師作為教學教材。

接二連三的開發危機與挫敗

  • 認識一位日本獨立遊戲開發者如何把勒索威脅化為宣傳機會，讓遊戲願望清單暴增。

摘要

Steam 與 Epic 的競爭，以及 AI 浪潮

作者指出，玩家熟悉 PlayStation 與 Xbox 的競爭，卻常覺得 PC 遊戲平台的角力早已一面倒：Steam 持續壯大，Epic Games 則始終難以追上。Steam 的同時在線人數創下新高，Epic 雖持續免費送遊戲，許多玩家領取後卻未必會玩；免費遊戲甚至可能間接帶動作品在 Steam 上的銷售。

生成式 AI 已經進入遊戲開發。Epic 執行長 Tim Sweeney 表示，公司正大幅轉型、運用 AI 提升開發效率與作品品質，並希望把相關優勢帶給 Unreal Engine 的開發團隊。他強調 AI 並非要取代員工，但外界看法分歧：有人認為 AI 是產業未來，也有人擔心它搶走工作，讓遊戲充斥粗製濫造的內容。

Epic 誇耀啟動速度，Steam 默默更新

Epic 宣布運用 AI 協助更新啟動器程式碼，聲稱啟動速度勝過「另一家平台」，明顯是在暗指 Steam。玩家卻不買帳，認為選擇 Steam 的原因遠不只是啟動速度，還有人以「垃圾桶開得再快，也不代表想吃裡面的東西」譏諷 Epic。更巧的是，Steam 隨後更新啟動效能與成就系統，社群測試認為速度已追平甚至略勝 Epic，令 Epic 的宣傳顯得尷尬。
